title: Weekly Update - Cross-play Issues, Recent Fixes, Upcoming Updates & More! - RuneScape Dragonwilds
author: IAmWaved
chapters: Cross-play Issues, Scorned Wilderness & Fix Timeline
description:
This weekly episode for #runescapedragonwilds covers the recent hotfix which bought along issues with the Scorned Wilderness Raid & Cross-play, whilst also fixing some of the recent problems caused by our latest major update last week.

We also touch on what updates we can expect for the rest of the year, the 2027 roadmap, and the devs plans to continue with year long sagas right through to 2030 and possibly beyond.

transcript.text: Hello folks, and welcome back to another Dragon Wild's weekly update video. Today we're covering the much anticipated
hotfix that arrived yesterday, fixing things like the air staff and stack splitting bugs. However, also causing an
entirely new issue for players, making the Scorned Wilderness raid and now cross-play for all platforms
unavailable. We do have some fixes for this already live, and then an outline for when it all will be finally
resolved. But then, beyond this, we have some info regarding the November and December updates, as well as the 2027
roadmap, and the devs' plans to drop a new saga each year right up to and possibly beyond the year 2030. As usual,
plenty for us to get through, and we are not wasting any time, so let's get started. Okay, so first things first, as of
today, we've had reports of issues with the Scorned Wilderness raid, in which players are falling through the floor
when being teleported by Commander Zyana. For now, the devs have flat-out said, "Until we've secured a fix, we do
not recommend tackling the Scorned Wilderness raid." But then, they followed this up just an hour or so
later with the following announcement, "Hello everyone, we'll be applying a fix to resolve the outstanding issue with
the Coldarra boss encounter. We will be rolling this patch out to console platforms as quickly as possible. We are
not waiting for each respective console platform before shipping this patch. This will mean that platforms on
mismatched patches will not be able to cross-play together. We cannot guarantee a timeline for when each platform gets
their respective patch due to console verification timelines. So, we appreciate your patience." This was then
followed up later on yesterday with an update that goes as follows, "Hello adventurers, Steam and Epic Games Store
players, the update should be available to you now. Jagex launcher users, this update will become available in roughly
45 minutes. Dedicated servers will need to be restarted to apply the hotfix. And then, the final post last night about
this revealed that PlayStation 5 players do now have the update, too, whereas Xbox users are still in the approval
stages, and they will announce when they have more information. And then, finally, keep in mind cross-play will
not be available whilst platforms are on different patches. And then, for Switch
two players, this update will not become available until next week. Now, this obviously isn't great news, as currently
the Scorned Wilderness Raid is the end game content everyone is getting their teeth into or working towards. And as a
result of it being an issue, crossplay for even those who aren't partaking or at the point of accessing the Scorned
Wilderness Raid just yet, will still be affected. This is all temporary, as just like every other issue we've had, it
will eventually get sorted. And as they say, they're rolling it out for each platform as fast as they can. PC and
PlayStation users are now of course fixed. It's likely Xbox will receive the update any moment now, as it could
actually already be out by the time you watch this video. So, do keep an eye out for a pinned comment below. However, as
mentioned, Switch users will be unable to crossplay until sometime next week. Make of all of this what you will, but
I'll likely circle back to it again and re-address it if we have any further issues. Now, prior to these issues and
definitely what caused them in the first place, would be the recent hotfix we were expecting this week already. It
arrived to just mere hours before this issue began, and it goes as follows. Hello adventurers, our 1.0.1.2
update is now live on all platforms. Dedicated servers will need to be restarted to apply the hotfix. Fix for
the air magic staff attack combos fourth hit not dealing damage or applying on hit effects. Splitting stacks with a
controller when the item's in a chest no longer causes a hitch where the controller becomes unresponsive. Fix for
rune crafting values being defaulted to one out of 50 whenever an amulet or ring degraded or lost durability. Fix Xbox
Series X hosted worlds not being able to support more than one Xbox client joining the world at a time. Additional
fixes for Kudra skips. Resolved an issue where users would lose progress when players with the same display name would
try and fail to log in. Fixed an issue where the dragon simitar would not allow users to jump attack in certain
circumstances. Fixed for silent quests where the quest UI would show them incorrectly, including calling missing
objective text. And then finally fix for Linux-based dedicated servers crashing when teleporting. Thanks for your
patience with us on this one. We'll be in touch very soon with the latest updates on all things 1.0.2 and what's
to come next month. Until then, be good and we'll see you in Ashen fall. Now, of
course, if you've been paying attention, then you'll begin to see a bit of a pattern. Most, if not all of the issues
fixed, like the air staff bug, splitting stacks, etc., were caused by the most recent major update just last week. And
then, upon fixing these, we have somewhat of a bigger issue with the Scorned Wilderness raid, indicating that
every update fixes things but breaks something else, which to some extent is absolutely true. But then, with all
things considered, we have a bunch of fixes here causing only one additional issue, and the devs are so forthcoming
and transparent with their acknowledgement of issues and outlining exactly what's being done about them
that I think they deserve some slack. Dragon Wilds is clearly a project that with time they've become more and more
comfortable developing and upgrading. It truly is a really fun and enjoyable experience of a game, and I'm sure if
these issues could have been avoided, they absolutely would have been. Regardless of how you may feel yourself,
at the very least things are constantly addressed and fixes are clearly outlined and communicated, which is about the
best we could hope for with any developer. Again, make of all of this what you will, and I'll circle back to
the entire subject again in the next weekly update video. Now, the next thing I wanted to discuss for today would be
the next major update we receive sometime next month. Previously, I had said that the October, November, and
December major updates are all technically part of the Luminance update for the end of this year. And whilst
still technically true, it's likely we won't get any of the actual showcased Luminance content until the big update
in December. I say this because this October update we just had did not include anything previously shown off,
like the prayer skill, elves, the loot, harmony stones, fairy rings, etc. And whilst I wasn't necessarily expecting
the big stuff to arrive before December, it does appear that everything we already know is coming won't be arriving
until then. What that means for the November update though is quite interesting as if we look at what we
received in this October update, it gives us a good idea as to what to expect next. This recent update included
a new special attack for all free ranged weapon types as well as a passive ammo recovery skill. We had a jump attack
included, separate slots for ring and amulets instead of just an accessory slot, increased inventory space and then
various other things here and there meaning that while still not as exciting or as big as the December update will
be, we can still expect a bunch of new things and improvements sometime in November. Naturally, as mentioned, this
will be followed by the massive luminous content update in December and then as of that point we begin going into 2027
starting an entirely new year-long saga and its first three-month chapter being Song of Rebellion. We won't get too
bogged down with the 2027 roadmap today as I've covered it a fair bit already and will likely dive into it a whole lot
more as we get closer to it actually arriving. What I do want to say though is this saga is basically made up of
four major content updates likely arriving in March, June, September and then December again, but then we'll also
have these monthly updates in between like the recent October update and upcoming November update. Beyond this,
we do of course have no idea what specifically comes next, but we did have it confirmed in a recent interview with
the devs that they plan to run year-long sagas right through to the year 2030 and
beyond. This plan could change a lot as the years go by so who knows how it will truly go, but at least for now we have
confirmation that the devs plan to update this game every month for a great many years to come. Now in summary
folks, PC and PlayStation players have had the recent issues fixed, Xbox players should be fixed any moment now
and then Switch 2 users will need to wait until sometime next week. We will receive more of these hot fixes that
I'll circle back to periodically as the next few weeks go by, but otherwise we are now waiting for the next big update
in November which we probably won't get any further details on until it actually arrives. Beyond this, there are of
course big plans for December, which may have more details revealed as and when we get closer, but generally consider
yourself very much brought up to speed on all things going on right now. I will be back next week with another weekly
update and possibly one or two other videos depending. And so of course that is then basically to say that do feel
free to treat this channel as your one-stop spot for all things RuneScape Dragon Wars moving forward. Anyway, that
would be it for this one, folks. I'll be back soon with plenty more, and I do of course have a range of guide and news
videos on the channel already, so do feel free to stop on by and check things [music] out. Otherwise, thanks for
watching, folks, and until next time. Peace.
